learn.hook: Can your hands dance? Let us say a rhyme and move them!
points: A rhyme is a short poem with a fun beat.
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words.
Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
We say a rhyme slowly and clearly, with a happy voice.

example.q: Read the rhyme: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap. Tap your knees, tap, tap, tap. Up they go and down they go. Wave to friends and say hello!" Which word rhymes with clap?
steps: Say clap. It ends with the sound -ap.
Say tap. It also ends with -ap.
So clap and tap rhyme.

learn.reallife: We say action rhymes in the school assembly and at home with Nani and Dadi.

items.text: Up they go and ___ they go.

games.title: True or false?
items: Clap and tap are rhyming words.
Go and hello are rhyming words.
Hand and cat are rhyming words.
Hand ends with -and. Cat ends with -at.
In an action rhyme, we move as we say it.
We do the actions, like clapping and waving.
In the rhyme, the hands say goodbye.
The hands wave and say hello.

quiz.q: Read: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap." What do the hands do?
quiz.explain: The line says the hands go clap, clap, clap.
steps: Read the line: clap your hands, clap, clap, clap.
The action word is clap.
So the hands clap.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the action word in the line

quiz.q: Read: "Wave to friends and say hello!" What do we say to friends?
quiz.explain: The line says: say hello.
steps: Read the line: wave to friends and say hello.
The word after say is hello.
So we say hello.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with tap?
quiz.explain: Tap and map both end with the sound -ap.
steps: Say tap. It ends with -ap.
Say map. It also ends with -ap.
So map rhymes with tap. Top starts like tap but ends with -op.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same will rhyme

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with go?
quiz.explain: Go and no both end with the sound -o.
steps: Say go. It ends with -o.
Say no. It also ends with -o.
So no rhymes with go. Got ends with -ot.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first letter, not the ending sound

quiz.q: Read: "Up they go and down they go." Which word is the opposite of up?
quiz.explain: Up and down are opposites.
steps: Up means high. The line says up they go and down they go.
Down means low.
So the opposite of up is down.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the opposite of up

quiz.q: How many hands do we clap together?
quiz.explain: We clap two hands together. One hand cannot clap on its own.
steps: We have two hands.
We clap them together.
So we clap 2 hands.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of hands with fingers

teach.ask: Gappu: What is an action rhyme? How do I say one?
teach.praise: Clap, clap! Now I can say an action rhyme!
teach.nudge: What do we do with our hands while we say the rhyme?

revise.summary: An action rhyme is a short, fun poem. We do the actions as we say it. Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
focus: Read a line and find the action in it
Find words that rhyme by their ending sound
Say a rhyme slowly and clearly
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound: clap, tap, map; go, no
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words
traps: Don't look at the first letter to find a rhyme. Look at the ending sound.
Top does not rhyme with tap. Map does.

learn.hook: Your body is like a busy team. Each part has a job!
points: We see with our eyes and hear with our ears.
We smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
We hold things with our hands and walk with our legs.
We have one nose, two eyes, two ears and two hands.

example.q: Think it through: I want to smell a rose. Which body part do I use?
steps: Smelling is the job of the nose.
Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells.
So I use my nose.

learn.reallife: When we wash up in the morning, we clean our face, eyes, ears, hands and feet.

games.title: Match the part to its job

quiz.q: Which body part do we use to see a kite?
quiz.explain: We see things with our eyes.
steps: Eyes see. Ears hear. Nose smells.
To see a kite, we use our eyes.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up seeing with hearing

quiz.q: Meena hears a bird sing. Which part helps her hear?
quiz.explain: We hear sounds with our ears.
steps: Hearing is the job of the ears.
So Meena hears the bird with her ears.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hearing with seeing

quiz.q: How many noses do you have?
quiz.explain: We have just one nose, in the middle of the face.
steps: Touch your face. There is one nose in the middle.
So we have 1 nose. We have two eyes, but only one nose.
quiz.mistake: Thinks we have two of every body part

quiz.q: 🖐️ Which is the right spelling for this body part?
quiz.explain: We spell it h-a-n-d: hand.
steps: Say the sounds: h-a-n-d.
Put them in order: hand.
Hnad has the n and a mixed up. Hend has e in place of a.
Answer: hand
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of letters

quiz.q: Nose begins with the letter ___.
quiz.explain: Nose begins with the sound n, so the letter is n.
steps: Say nose. The first sound is n.
So nose begins with n, not m.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the letters n and m

quiz.q: Which body part tastes a sweet laddoo?
quiz.explain: We taste food with our tongue.
steps: We taste food with our tongue.
So the tongue tastes the sweet laddoo.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which part tastes

teach.ask: Gappu: I have so many body parts! What do they all do?
teach.praise: Wow! Now I know my eyes see and my ears hear!
teach.nudge: What do eyes and ears do?

revise.summary: Each body part has a job. We see with our eyes, hear with our ears, smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
focus: Match each body part to its job
Know how many of each part we have
Spell body words like hand and nose
remember: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes
Hands hold things, legs walk
One nose, two eyes, two ears, two hands
traps: Don't think we have two of every part. We have only one nose.
Don't mix up seeing (eyes) with hearing (ears).

learn.hook: Jump! Run! Clap! These words make you move!
points: Some words tell us what we do. They are action words, or doing words.
Run, jump, clap, eat, sleep and write are action words.
We write with our hands. We kick with our feet.
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.

example.q: Think it through: In "Ravi kicks the ball", which is the action word?
steps: Ask: what does Ravi do?
Ravi kicks.
So kicks is the action word.

learn.reallife: In PT class, the teacher says: run, jump, stop! These are action words.

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

items.q: With a ball and your feet, you ___
With a glass of milk, you ___
With two hands at a show, you ___

quiz.q: Which is an action word?
quiz.explain: Jump tells us what we do. Hand is a body part. Red is a colour.
steps: An action word tells what we do.
We can jump. So jump is an action word.
Hand is a body part. Red is a colour.
Answer: Jump
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word instead of a doing word

quiz.q: Read: "Asha claps her hands." Which word is the action word?
quiz.explain: Claps tells what Asha does.
steps: Ask: what does Asha do?
Asha claps. So claps is the action word.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word instead of the action

quiz.q: What do we do with a pencil?
quiz.explain: We hold a pencil and write with it.
steps: We hold a pencil in our hand.
We write with a pencil.
quiz.mistake: Matches the wrong action to the thing

quiz.q: I ___ my teeth every morning.
quiz.explain: We brush our teeth every morning.
steps: Every morning we clean our teeth.
We brush our teeth. So the word is brush.
quiz.mistake: Picks an action that does not fit the sentence

quiz.q: Which action do we do with our legs?
quiz.explain: We run with our legs. We eat with our mouth and hear with our ears.
steps: Our legs help us move.
We run with our legs. We eat with our mouth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which body part does the action

quiz.q: Which is NOT an action word?
quiz.explain: Chair is the name of a thing. Sing and hop are things we do.
steps: Sing and hop are things we do.
Chair is the name of a thing.
So chair is NOT an action word.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every word is an action word

teach.ask: Gappu: What is an action word? Is chair one?
teach.praise: Hop, hop! I know action words now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me some things we do, like run or jump?

revise.summary: Action words, or doing words, tell us what we do, like run, jump, clap, eat and write.
focus: Pick the action word in a sentence
Tell action words apart from naming words
Match an action to the body part that does it
remember: Action words: run, jump, clap, eat, sleep, write
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.
Ask 'What does he or she do?' to find the action word
traps: Don't pick a naming word like hand or chair as the action word.
Don't match the wrong body part: we write with hands, kick with feet.

topics.title: Polite words: good morning, thank you

learn.hook: Magic words make everyone smile. Do you know them?
points: We say good morning when we meet someone in the morning.
We say good afternoon after 12 noon and good evening in the evening.
We say good night when we go to bed.
Please, thank you and sorry are magic words.
We say thank you when someone helps us or gives us something.

example.q: Think it through: Dadi gives Tara a glass of milk. What should Tara say?
steps: Dadi gave Tara something.
When someone gives us something, we say thank you.
So Tara says, "Thank you, Dadi!"

learn.reallife: At school we say "Good morning, ma'am" to our teacher. At home we say "Please" when we ask for more dal.

games.title: When do we say it?
pairs: when we meet someone in the morning

games.title: True or false?
items: We say good morning when the day begins.
Good morning is the greeting for the morning.
We say good night when we wake up.
We say good night when we go to bed.
We say sorry when we hurt someone by mistake.
Sorry shows we feel bad about it.
Please is a polite word to use when we ask for something.
"May I have water, please?" is polite.
We say thank you when we push a friend.
Pushing is not kind. We say sorry if we push someone.

quiz.q: Ria meets her teacher at 8 in the morning. What should she say?
quiz.explain: In the morning, we say good morning.
steps: Ria meets her teacher at 8 in the morning.
In the morning, we say good morning.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the greetings for different times of day

quiz.q: Amit is going to bed. What does he say to Mummy?
quiz.explain: We say good night when we go to bed.
steps: Amit is going to bed.
When we go to bed, we say good night.
quiz.mistake: Thinks good night is said when we wake up

quiz.q: Your friend gives you a pencil. What do you say?
quiz.explain: When someone gives us something, we say thank you.
steps: Your friend gives you a pencil.
When someone gives us something, we say thank you. Sorry is for a mistake.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up thank you and sorry

quiz.q: Kabir steps on Neha's foot by mistake. What should he say?
quiz.explain: We say sorry when we make a mistake or hurt someone.
steps: Kabir stepped on Neha's foot by mistake.
When we make a mistake or hurt someone, we say sorry.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when to say sorry

quiz.q: Which is the polite way to ask?
options: May I have a laddoo, please?
quiz.explain: Using please and may I is polite.
steps: Please and may I are polite words.
So 'May I have a laddoo, please?' is the polite way. The others are orders.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a loud order is polite

quiz.q: It is 2 o'clock in the afternoon. You meet Nani. What do you say?
quiz.explain: After 12 noon and before evening, we say good afternoon.
steps: 2 o'clock is after 12 noon and before evening.
So we say good afternoon.
quiz.mistake: Thinks good morning is used all day

teach.ask: Gappu: What are magic words? When do I say good morning?
teach.praise: Thank you! Now I know my magic words!
teach.nudge: What do I say when someone helps me?

revise.summary: We greet people by the time of day: good morning, good afternoon, good evening and good night. Please, thank you and sorry are magic words.
focus: Pick the right greeting for the time of day
Know when to say please, thank you and sorry
Ask for things in a polite way
remember: Morning: good morning. After 12 noon: good afternoon. Evening: good evening. Bed time: good night.
Say thank you when someone helps you or gives you something
Say sorry when you make a mistake or hurt someone
traps: Don't say good morning all day. After 12 noon it is good afternoon.
Good night is for going to bed, not for waking up.
Don't mix up thank you and sorry.

learn.hook: Hello! What is your name? Let us talk nicely!
points: When we meet a friend, we can say hello or namaste.
We ask "How are you?" and answer "I am fine, thank you."
We say "My name is ..." to tell our name.
We say bye or goodbye when we leave.
We speak kindly and wait for our turn to talk.

example.q: Read: Raju: "Hello! What is your name?" Gita: "My name is Gita." Raju: "How are you, Gita?" What should Gita say now?
steps: Raju asked how Gita is.
A polite answer to "How are you?" is "I am fine, thank you."
Gita can also ask, "And you?"

learn.reallife: When a guest comes home, we say namaste or hello and ask, "How are you?"

games.title: Put the talk in order
games.prompt: Put the talk in the right order.
items: Sam: Hello, Meena! How are you?
Meena: I am fine, thank you. And you?

items.text: It is time to go. ___, Dadu!

quiz.q: Read: "Hello! My name is Zoya." What is the girl's name?
quiz.explain: She says, "My name is Zoya."
steps: The girl says, 'My name is Zoya.'
The word after 'My name is' is her name: Zoya.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word from the line that is not a name

quiz.q: Your friend asks, "How are you?" What is a good answer?
quiz.explain: "I am fine, thank you" answers "How are you?"
steps: 'How are you?' asks how you feel.
So we answer, 'I am fine, thank you.'
quiz.mistake: Gives an answer to a different question

quiz.q: You are leaving your friend's house. What do you say?
quiz.explain: When we leave, we say bye or goodbye.
steps: You are leaving.
When we leave, we say bye or goodbye.
Answer: Bye! See you soon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up words for meeting and leaving

quiz.q: Which question asks for a name?
quiz.explain: "What is your name?" asks for a name.
steps: We want to know a name.
So we ask, 'What is your name?'
quiz.mistake: Mixes up different questions

quiz.q: Papa is talking on the phone. What should you do?
quiz.explain: It is polite to wait for our turn to speak.
steps: Papa is talking. It is his turn to speak.
It is polite to wait for him to finish.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about waiting for a turn

quiz.q: Which is a kind way to greet Dadi?
quiz.explain: Namaste and "How are you?" are kind and polite.
steps: Namaste is a kind greeting.
'Namaste, Dadi! How are you?' is kind and polite. The others are rude.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rude words are a greeting

teach.ask: Gappu: I met a new friend! What do I say to her?
teach.praise: Hello, friend! Now I can talk nicely!
teach.nudge: What do I say first when I meet my friend?

revise.summary: We say hello or namaste when we meet, tell our name, ask 'How are you?' and say bye when we leave. We speak kindly and wait for our turn.
focus: Greet family and friends in a kind way
Answer 'How are you?' and 'What is your name?'
Know words for meeting and for leaving
remember: Meeting: hello, namaste. Leaving: bye, goodbye.
'How are you?' - 'I am fine, thank you.'
'What is your name?' - 'My name is ...'
traps: Don't answer 'How are you?' with your name.
Don't say good morning when you leave. Say bye.
Don't talk when someone else is talking. Wait for your turn.

learn.hook: Look closely! A picture is full of tiny stories.
points: First look at the whole picture. Then look at each part.
Say what you see: "I can see a cat."
Tell the colour and size: "I can see a big red ball."
Tell how many: "I can see two birds."
Tell where: "The cat is under the tree."

example.q: Look: 🌳🐒🐒🐒 (three monkeys near a tree). Tell about the picture in one sentence.
steps: What do I see? Monkeys and a tree.
How many monkeys? Count: 1, 2, 3.
Put it together in a sentence.
example.answer: I can see three monkeys near a tree.

learn.reallife: When Dadu shows us old photos, we tell him who we see and what they are doing.

games.title: Picture talk: true or false?
items: "I can see a cat" tells what is in a picture.
It names the thing we see.
An elephant is smaller than an ant.
An elephant is big. An ant is small.
Big and small tell about size.
They tell how large a thing is.
🌞 is a picture of the moon.

quiz.q: Look: 🐄🐄. How many cows can you see?
quiz.explain: Count the cows: 1, 2. There are two cows.
steps: Count the cows: 1, 2.
There are 2 cows.
quiz.mistake: Counts wrongly

quiz.q: Look: 🐦🐦🐦🐦 on a wire. How many birds?
quiz.explain: Count: 1, 2, 3, 4. There are four birds.
steps: Count the birds: 1, 2, 3, 4.
There are 4 birds.
quiz.mistake: Skips or repeats while counting

quiz.q: Look: 🐘 and 🐭. Which one is big?
quiz.explain: An elephant is big. A mouse is small.
steps: An elephant is very big. A mouse is very small.
So the elephant is big.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up big and small

quiz.q: Which sentence tells about 🌳🐱 (a cat under a tree)?
options: The cat is on the moon.
The cat is under the tree.
The tree is in the cat.
quiz.explain: The cat sits under the tree, so we say "under the tree".
steps: Look at the picture. The cat is below the tree.
So we say, 'The cat is under the tree.'
quiz.mistake: Does not match the words to the picture

quiz.q: Look: 🎈 (a red balloon). Which word tells its colour?
quiz.explain: Red is a colour word.
steps: Red tells us the colour.
Round tells the shape. Balloon is the name.
Answer: Red
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape word or naming word for colour

quiz.q: What is a good way to start telling about a picture?
quiz.explain: "I can see" tells what is in the picture.
steps: We tell what is in the picture.
So we begin with 'I can see ...'
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to begin describing

teach.ask: Gappu: My Nani sent me a picture. How do I tell about it?
teach.praise: I can see a happy Gappu! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Can I tell the colour, size or how many?

revise.summary: To tell about a picture, look at the whole picture first, then say what you see, its colour and size, how many and where it is.
focus: Count things in a picture
Tell colour, size and place
Make a sentence that begins 'I can see ...'
remember: Begin with: I can see ...
Tell colour and size: I can see a big red ball.
Tell where: The cat is under the tree.
traps: Don't skip or count twice when you count.
Don't mix up a colour word (red) with a shape word (round).

learn.hook: Everything has a name. Even your toothbrush!
points: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing.
Cat, cow, parrot and tiger are names of animals.
Bag, cup, ball and chair are names of things.
We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds: an apple, an egg, an owl.
We use a before other sounds: a cat, a bag, a dog.

example.q: Think it through: Is it "a egg" or "an egg"?
steps: Say egg. It begins with the e sound.
a, e, i, o, u are vowels.
We use an before a vowel sound.

learn.reallife: In the kitchen we can name many things: a cup, a plate, a spoon and an onion!

quiz.q: Which is the name of an animal?
quiz.explain: A tiger is an animal. A table and a pencil are things.
steps: A tiger is an animal.
A table and a pencil are things.
Answer: Tiger
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animals and things

quiz.q: Which is the name of a thing?
quiz.explain: We eat with a spoon. It is a thing, not an animal.
steps: A spoon is a thing. We eat with it.
A goat and a peacock are animals.
Answer: Spoon
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animals and things

quiz.q: 🍎 Choose the right words for this picture.
quiz.explain: Apple begins with the a sound, a vowel. So we say an apple.
steps: Say apple. It begins with the a sound.
A, e, i, o, u are vowels. We use an before a vowel sound.
One apple, so: an apple.
quiz.mistake: Uses a before a vowel sound

quiz.q: 🐕 Which words name this pet the right way?
quiz.explain: Dog begins with d, not a vowel. So we say a dog.
steps: Say dog. It begins with d. D is not a vowel.
We use a before other sounds. One dog, so: a dog.
quiz.mistake: Uses an before every word

quiz.q: Read: "The parrot sits on a branch." Which word names a bird?
quiz.explain: Parrot is the name of a bird.
steps: A parrot is a bird.
Sits is an action word. So parrot names the bird.
quiz.mistake: Picks an action word instead of a naming word

quiz.q: ⚽ Which is the right spelling for this toy?
quiz.explain: We spell it b-a-l-l: ball.
steps: Say the sounds: b-a-l-l.
Ball has two l letters at the end: ball.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out a letter or uses the wrong vowel

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a naming word? And when do I say an?
teach.praise: An excellent answer! I mean, a great answer!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me some names of animals or things?

revise.summary: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing. We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds and a before other sounds.
focus: Sort names into animals and things
Choose a or an before a word
Spell naming words like ball
remember: an apple, an egg, an owl (a, e, i, o, u sounds)
a cat, a bag, a dog (other sounds)
Animals: cat, cow, parrot, tiger. Things: bag, cup, ball, chair.
traps: Don't say 'a apple'. Say an apple.
Don't use an before every word. It is a dog.

chapters.title: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys

learn.hook: Shh! Story time! Grandparents know the best old stories.
points: The lesson is a funny folk tale about a cap seller and some naughty monkeys.
A folk tale is an old story. People tell it again and again.
The people and animals in a story are its characters.
When we listen, we look at the speaker and stay quiet.
Here is our own story: Raju and the Bell.

example.q: Listen: "Raju had a shiny red bell. He sat under a neem tree to rest. Mini the monkey took the bell and climbed up the tree. Mini copies everything she sees. Raju had an idea. He clapped his hands. Mini clapped too! The bell fell down, and Raju picked it up." Who are the characters?
steps: Who is in the story? Raju is in it.
A monkey named Mini is in it.
So the characters are Raju and Mini.

learn.reallife: At bedtime, Nani or Dadi may tell us an old story they heard when they were small.

games.title: Raju and the Bell: true or false?
items: In the story, Raju had a red bell.
The story says: Raju had a shiny red bell.
In the story, Raju sat under a neem tree.
He sat under a neem tree to rest.
In the story, a cat took the bell.
Mini the monkey took the bell.
In the story, Mini copies what she sees.
The story says Mini copies everything she sees.
At the end of the story, the bell is lost.
The bell fell down and Raju picked it up.

quiz.q: Read: "Raju had a shiny red bell." What colour was the bell?
quiz.explain: The line says the bell was shiny and red.
steps: Read the line: a shiny red bell.
The colour word is red.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the colour word

quiz.q: Read: "He sat under a neem tree to rest." Where did Raju sit?
quiz.explain: The line says he sat under a neem tree.
steps: Read the line: he sat under a neem tree.
So Raju sat under a neem tree.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Read: "Mini the monkey took the bell." Who took the bell?
quiz.explain: The line says Mini the monkey took it.
steps: Read the line: Mini the monkey took the bell.
So Mini the monkey took it, not Raju.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the characters

quiz.q: What is a folk tale?
options: An old story told again and again
quiz.explain: Folk tales are old stories passed on by people.
steps: A folk tale is an old story.
People tell it again and again.
Answer: An old story told again and again
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a folk tale is

quiz.q: How should we listen to a story?
quiz.explain: Good listeners stay quiet and look at the speaker.
steps: Good listeners stay quiet.
They look at the speaker.
Answer: Quietly, looking at the speaker
quiz.mistake: Does not know good listening manners

quiz.q: Read: "Mini climbed up the tree." Climbed up means Mini went ___.
quiz.explain: Climbing up means going higher.
steps: Up means to a high place.
So climbed up means Mini went higher.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up up and down

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a folk tale? Who was in our story?
teach.praise: What a lovely story! I want to hear it again!
teach.nudge: Who was in the story? What did they do?

revise.summary: A folk tale is an old story that people tell again and again. The people and animals in it are its characters. We listen quietly and look at the speaker.
focus: Find who is in a story (the characters)
Read a line and answer what, who and where
Know good listening manners
remember: Folk tale: an old story told again and again
Characters: the people and animals in a story
In Raju and the Bell, the characters are Raju and Mini the monkey
traps: Don't guess. Read the line to find the answer.
Don't mix up the characters: Mini took the bell, not Raju.

learn.hook: Monkey see, monkey do! Can you copy a funny face?
points: To copy means to do the same thing as someone else.
In the lesson, the monkeys copy the cap seller.
Clever means quick at thinking of good ideas.
Raju was clever. He knew Mini would copy him.

example.q: Think it through: Raju clapped. Mini clapped too. Why did the bell fall?
steps: Mini was holding the bell.
She copied Raju and clapped her hands.
To clap, she let go of the bell, so it fell.
example.answer: Mini let go of the bell to copy Raju's clap.

learn.reallife: When we play "Simon says" or "Follow the leader", we copy the leader.

quiz.q: Raju waves. Mini waves too. What is Mini doing?
quiz.explain: Doing the same as someone else is copying.
steps: Raju waves. Mini does the same thing.
Doing the same as someone else is copying.
Answer: Copying Raju
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of copy

quiz.q: Which word means quick at thinking of good ideas?
quiz.explain: A clever person thinks of good ideas quickly.
steps: Clever means quick at thinking of good ideas.
Lazy and sleepy do not mean that.
Answer: Clever
quiz.mistake: Mixes up describing words

quiz.q: Raju knew Mini copies everything. Then he clapped. Why did he clap?
options: He knew Mini would copy him
quiz.explain: Raju wanted Mini to copy him and drop the bell.
steps: Raju knew Mini copies everything.
He clapped so that Mini would copy him and drop the bell.
quiz.mistake: Misses the reason in the story

quiz.q: Which is the opposite of up?
quiz.explain: Up and down are opposites.
steps: Up means high.
Down means low. So down is the opposite of up.
quiz.mistake: Does not know opposites

quiz.q: Read: "Mini took the bell." The opposite of took is ___.
quiz.explain: Take and give are opposites. Took and gave are opposites too.
steps: Took means Mini got the bell.
The opposite is to hand it over: gave. Got means almost the same as took.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with a similar meaning

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with cap?
quiz.explain: Cap and map both end with the sound -ap.
steps: Say cap. It ends with -ap.
Say map. It also ends with -ap. So map rhymes with cap.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first letters

teach.ask: Gappu: What does copy mean? Why was Raju clever?
teach.praise: Clever you! I will copy your good idea!
teach.nudge: What does it mean to copy someone?

revise.summary: To copy means to do the same thing as someone else. Raju was clever: he knew Mini would copy him, so he clapped and Mini dropped the bell.
focus: Know the meaning of copy and clever
Tell why things happen in the story
Find opposites and rhyming words
remember: Copy: do the same thing as someone else
Clever: quick at thinking of good ideas
Opposites: up and down, took and gave
traps: Don't pick a word with the same meaning when asked for the opposite: got is not the opposite of took.
Cup does not rhyme with cap. Map does.

learn.hook: Stories are like a train. Each part comes in its turn!
points: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
We use first, next, then and last to tell a story in order.
If we mix up the order, the story does not make sense.

example.q: Put in order: (a) The bell fell down. (b) Mini took the bell. (c) Raju clapped his hands.
steps: First, Mini took the bell.
Next, Raju clapped his hands.
Last, the bell fell down.

learn.reallife: We get ready in order: first we wake up, then we brush, then we bathe, then we eat.

quiz.q: Story: Raju sat under a tree. Mini took the bell. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened first?
quiz.explain: The story begins with Raju resting under a tree.
steps: Read the story from the start.
The first thing is: Raju sat under a tree.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the beginning and the end

quiz.q: Story: Mini took the bell. Raju clapped. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened last?
quiz.explain: At the end, the bell fell and Raju picked it up.
steps: Look at the end of the story.
The last thing is: Raju picked up the bell.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the beginning and the end

quiz.q: Raju clapped. Mini copies everything she sees. What did Mini do next?
options: Mini ran away with the bell
quiz.explain: Mini copied Raju and clapped.
steps: Mini copies everything she sees.
Raju clapped, so next Mini clapped too.
quiz.mistake: Does not follow the story order

quiz.q: Which word tells the end of a list of steps?
quiz.explain: Last comes at the end.
steps: First is at the start. Next is in the middle.
Last is at the end.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up first and last

quiz.q: First I wake up. Next I brush my teeth. Then I ___.
quiz.explain: After waking and brushing, we eat breakfast.
steps: Wake up, then brush teeth.
After that, we eat breakfast. Going to bed comes at night.
quiz.mistake: Repeats a step or jumps to the end of the day

quiz.q: Which comes first in a story?
quiz.explain: A story starts with the beginning.
steps: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
The beginning comes first.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the parts of a story

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I tell a story in the right order?
teach.praise: First you taught me, then I learnt, and last I said thank you!
teach.nudge: Which words help us tell a story in order?

revise.summary: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. We use first, next, then and last to tell it in the right order.
focus: Say what happened first and what happened last
Put story events in order
Use first, next, then and last
remember: Order words: first, next, then, last
A story has a beginning, a middle and an end
traps: Don't mix up first and last.
Don't jump ahead. If the order is mixed up, the story does not make sense.

learn.hook: Cock-a-doodle-doo! Wake up, the farm is busy!
points: A farm has fields, and animals like cows, goats, hens, ducks and horses.
A cow gives us milk. A hen lays eggs.
A sheep gives us wool to make warm sweaters.
Baby animals have their own names: a calf, a chick, a puppy, a kitten.

example.q: Think it through: Which farm animal gives us milk for our chai?
steps: Milk comes from cows (and from buffaloes and goats too).
Hens give eggs, not milk.
So a cow is a good answer.

learn.reallife: Dahi, paneer and ghee are made from milk. Many families in villages keep cows and buffaloes.

games.title: Farm facts: true or false?
items: A baby cow is called a calf.
A young cow is a calf.
We get wool from a duck.
A baby cat is called a puppy.
A baby cat is a kitten. A baby dog is a puppy.
Cows eat grass and green fodder.

quiz.q: Which animal lays eggs?
quiz.explain: A hen lays eggs.
steps: A hen lays eggs.
A cow gives milk. A horse does not lay eggs.
Answer: Hen
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which animal gives what

quiz.q: What do we get from sheep?
quiz.explain: Sheep give wool. It is used to make sweaters.
steps: A sheep gives us wool.
Wool is used to make warm sweaters.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which animal gives what

quiz.q: A baby dog is called a ___.
quiz.explain: A baby dog is a puppy.
steps: Baby animals have their own names.
A baby dog is a puppy. A kitten is a baby cat. A calf is a baby cow.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up baby animal names

quiz.q: Read: "The ducks go quack beside the lake." Where are the ducks?
quiz.explain: The line says the ducks are beside the lake.
steps: Read the line: the ducks go quack beside the lake.
So the ducks are beside the lake.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Read: "Off goes Dadu in his truck!" How does Dadu go?
quiz.explain: The line says Dadu goes in his truck.
steps: Read to the end of the line: off goes Dadu in his truck.
So Dadu goes in his truck.
quiz.mistake: Does not read to the end of the line

quiz.q: Which one is a farm animal?
quiz.explain: Goats live on farms. Sharks live in the sea and penguins live in very cold places.
steps: A goat lives on a farm.
A shark lives in the sea. A penguin lives in very cold places.
Answer: Goat
quiz.mistake: Mixes up farm animals with wild animals

teach.ask: Gappu: Which animals live on a farm? What do they give us?
teach.praise: Moo-velous! You know your farm friends!
teach.nudge: What does a cow or a hen give us?

revise.summary: A farm has fields and animals like cows, goats, hens, ducks and horses. A cow gives milk, a hen lays eggs and a sheep gives wool.
focus: Know which farm animal gives what
Know the names of baby animals
Tell farm animals apart from wild animals
remember: Cow: milk. Hen: eggs. Sheep: wool.
Baby animals: calf, chick, puppy, kitten
traps: Don't mix up which animal gives what: hens give eggs, not milk.
A shark is not a farm animal. It lives in the sea.

learn.hook: Moo! Quack! Baa! Who is talking?
points: Each animal makes its own sound.
A cow moos. A duck quacks. A hen clucks.
A dog barks. A cat mews (meows). A sheep says baa.
A horse neighs. A donkey brays: hee-haw!
A rooster crows: cock-a-doodle-doo!

example.q: Read the poem: "Hello, hello, the farm is awake! The ducks go quack beside the lake. The cow says moo, the hen says cluck, and off goes Dadu in his truck!" What does the hen say?
steps: Find the hen in the poem.
The poem says: the hen says cluck.
So the hen says cluck.

learn.reallife: In a village, the rooster crows early in the morning and wakes everyone up!

quiz.q: What sound does a duck make?
quiz.explain: Ducks say quack.
steps: Each animal makes its own sound.
A duck says quack.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animal sounds

quiz.q: Which animal says moo?
quiz.explain: A cow says moo.
steps: Moo is the sound of a cow.
A dog barks and a hen clucks.
Answer: Cow
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animal sounds

quiz.q: A dog ___.
quiz.explain: We say a dog barks.
steps: The word for a dog's sound is barks.
So: a dog barks.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animal sound words

quiz.q: Which animal says cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning?
quiz.explain: A rooster crows cock-a-doodle-doo.
steps: Cock-a-doodle-doo is the sound a rooster makes.
A rooster crows in the morning.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animal sounds

quiz.q: A horse ___.
quiz.explain: We say a horse neighs.
steps: The word for a horse's sound is neighs.
So: a horse neighs.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animal sound words

quiz.q: Read: "The cow says moo, the hen says cluck." Who says cluck?
quiz.explain: The line says the hen says cluck.
steps: Read the line: the hen says cluck.
So the hen says cluck. The cow says moo.
quiz.mistake: Reads the wrong part of the line

teach.ask: Gappu: Tweet! I can only tweet. What sounds do farm animals make?
teach.praise: Moo, quack, baa! What a noisy, happy farm!
teach.nudge: What does a cow say? What does a duck say?

revise.summary: Each animal makes its own sound. A cow moos, a duck quacks, a hen clucks, a dog barks and a horse neighs.
focus: Match each animal to its sound
Use the sound word in a sentence: a dog barks
Read a line to find who makes which sound
remember: Cow: moo. Duck: quack. Hen: cluck. Sheep: baa.
Dog barks. Cat mews. Horse neighs. Donkey brays.
Rooster crows: cock-a-doodle-doo!
traps: Don't mix up animal sounds: a dog barks, a cow moos.
Read the right part of the line to see who makes the sound.

learn.hook: Cat, hat, mat... Words that sound alike are fun!
points: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Cat, hat and mat rhyme. They all end with -at.
Hen, pen and ten rhyme. They all end with -en.
Words that only begin the same do not rhyme. Cat and cow do not rhyme.
Poems often use rhyming words at the end of lines.

example.q: Read: "The cow says moo, the hen says cluck, and off goes Dadu in his truck!" Which word rhymes with cluck?
steps: Cluck ends with the sound -uck.
Truck also ends with -uck.
So cluck and truck rhyme.

learn.reallife: Many songs and rhymes we sing at school have rhyming words, like star and are.

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with hen?
quiz.explain: Hen and ten both end with -en.
steps: Say hen. It ends with -en.
Ten also ends with -en. So ten rhymes with hen.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same will rhyme

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with cat?
quiz.explain: Cat and mat both end with -at.
steps: Say cat. It ends with -at.
Mat also ends with -at. Cow starts like cat but does not rhyme.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same will rhyme

quiz.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
quiz.explain: Dog and log both end with -og.
steps: Dog ends with -og. Log ends with -og too.
So dog and log rhyme. Dog and duck only start the same.
quiz.mistake: Picks words that begin with the same letter

quiz.q: Read: "The farm is awake! The ducks go quack beside the lake." Which word rhymes with awake?
quiz.explain: Awake and lake both end with the sound -ake.
steps: Awake ends with the sound -ake.
Lake also ends with -ake. So lake rhymes with awake.
quiz.mistake: Picks any word from the poem

quiz.q: Which word does NOT rhyme with pen?
quiz.explain: Pin ends with -in. Pen, ten and hen end with -en.
steps: Pen, ten and hen end with -en.
Pin ends with -in. So pin does NOT rhyme with pen.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the first letter instead of the ending

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with goat?
quiz.explain: Goat and coat both end with -oat.
steps: Goat ends with -oat.
Coat also ends with -oat. Gate starts like goat but ends with -ate.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same will rhyme

teach.ask: Gappu: My teacher says cat and hat rhyme. What does that mean?
teach.praise: Hat, cat, mat... I am a rhyming star!
teach.nudge: Do rhyming words sound the same at the start or at the end?

revise.summary: Rhyming words end with the same sound, like cat, hat and mat. Words that only begin the same, like cat and cow, do not rhyme.
focus: Find a word that rhymes by its ending sound
Spot the word that does not rhyme
Find rhyming words in a poem
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound
-at: cat, hat, mat. -en: hen, pen, ten.
Poems often have rhyming words at the end of lines
traps: Don't pick a word just because it starts the same. Cat and cow do not rhyme.
Pin does not rhyme with pen. Check the ending sound.

learn.hook: A picture can tell a story without any words!
points: To read a picture, we ask: Who? What? Where?
Who is in the picture? A girl, a dog, a bird...
What are they doing? Running, eating, flying...
Where are they? In a park, at home, near a river...
We can count the things we see.

example.q: Look: 👧⚽🌳 (a girl kicks a ball in a park). Who is it? What is she doing? Where is she?
steps: Who? A girl.
What is she doing? She is kicking a ball.
Where? In a park, near a tree.
example.answer: A girl is kicking a ball in a park.

learn.reallife: Signs on the road and in the bus use pictures, like a picture of a person walking.

games.title: Look and answer
items: A sparrow flaps its wings and flies.
Count them: 1, 2, 3. There are three cows.
🍌 is a picture of a carrot.

quiz.q: Look: 🐱🐱🐱 on a wall. How many cats?
quiz.explain: Count: 1, 2, 3. There are three cats.
steps: Count the cats: 1, 2, 3.
There are 3 cats.
quiz.mistake: Counts wrongly

quiz.q: Look: 🦋🦋🦋🦋🦋 near flowers. How many butterflies?
quiz.explain: Count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are five butterflies.
steps: Count the butterflies: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
There are 5 butterflies.
quiz.mistake: Skips or repeats while counting

quiz.q: Look: 👦📖 (a boy with a book). What is the boy doing?
quiz.explain: A boy with an open book is reading.
steps: Look: the boy has a book.
A boy with a book is reading.
quiz.mistake: Does not look closely at the picture

quiz.q: Look: 🐠 in a pond. Where is the fish?
quiz.explain: The fish is in the pond.
steps: Look: the fish is in water.
So the fish is in the pond.
quiz.mistake: Does not look at where the thing is

quiz.q: Which question asks about a place?
quiz.explain: Where asks about the place.
steps: Where asks about a place.
Who asks about a person. How many asks about a number.
Answer: Where?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up question words

quiz.q: Look: 👩‍🍳🍲 (Amma at the stove). Which word tells what she is doing?
quiz.explain: Amma is at the stove with a pot, so she is cooking.
steps: Amma is at the stove with a pot.
So she is cooking.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the clues in the picture

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I read a picture? It has no words!
teach.praise: Wow, pictures talk to me now!
teach.nudge: Which questions can I ask about a picture?

revise.summary: To read a picture, we ask Who? What? Where? We can also count the things we see.
focus: Answer who, what and where about a picture
Count the things in a picture
Use picture clues to tell what someone is doing
remember: Who? tells the person or animal
What? tells what they are doing
Where? tells the place
traps: Don't mix up question words: where asks about a place, not a person.
Don't skip or count twice when counting.

learn.hook: Red, blue, green! Round, square, three corners! Let us look around!
points: Red, blue, yellow, green, orange, pink, white and black are colours.
Grass is green. Milk is white. A crow is black.
A circle is round, like a roti or a coin.
A triangle has 3 sides. A square has 4 equal sides.
A rectangle has 4 sides, like a door or a book.

example.q: Think it through: A carrom board has 4 equal sides. What shape is it?
steps: Count the sides: 4.
All 4 sides are the same length.
A shape with 4 equal sides and square corners is a square.

learn.reallife: Look around: the clock is round, the door is a rectangle, and a slice of watermelon looks like a triangle.

quiz.q: What shape is a coin?
quiz.explain: A coin is round, so it is a circle.
steps: A coin is round.
A round shape is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up shape names

quiz.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
steps: Count the sides of a triangle: 1, 2, 3.
A square has 4 sides, but a triangle has 3.
Answer: 3
quiz.mistake: Mixes up triangle and square

quiz.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 sides, all the same length.
steps: A square has 4 sides.
All 4 sides are the same length.
Answer: Square
quiz.mistake: Mixes up shape names

quiz.q: A door has 4 sides. Two are long and two are short. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: A shape with 2 long and 2 short sides is a rectangle.
steps: A door has 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short.
That shape is a rectangle. A square has 4 equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every 4-sided shape is a square

quiz.q: What colour is grass?
quiz.explain: Grass is green.
steps: Look at grass.
Grass is green.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up colour names

quiz.q: Which is the right spelling for the colour of a ripe banana?
quiz.explain: We spell it y-e-l-l-o-w, with two l's.
steps: Say the letters: y-e-l-l-o-w.
Yellow has two l's: yellow.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out a letter or uses the wrong vowel

teach.ask: Gappu: What colours and shapes can you find around you?
teach.praise: What a colourful answer! I see shapes everywhere now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me a colour and a shape?

revise.summary: We know colours like red, blue, green and yellow, and shapes: a circle is round, a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 equal sides, and a rectangle has 2 long and 2 short sides.
focus: Name the shape of things we see
Count the sides of a shape
Know colours of things and spell colour words
remember: Circle: round, like a coin or a roti
Triangle: 3 sides. Square: 4 equal sides.
Rectangle: 4 sides, 2 long and 2 short, like a door
Grass is green. Milk is white. A crow is black.
traps: Don't call every 4-sided shape a square. A door is a rectangle.
Yellow has two l's.

learn.hook: A trip to the sabzi market! What will we buy?
points: Mango, banana, apple, guava, papaya and grapes are fruits.
Potato, carrot, spinach, onion, brinjal and cauliflower are vegetables.
Many fruits are sweet and we can eat them raw.
We cook many vegetables to make sabzi, dal or soup.
The mango is the national fruit of India.

example.q: Read: "Pinky goes to the market with Papa. She sees red apples and yellow bananas. Papa buys green spinach and orange carrots. Pinky picks a big mango. "Yum!" she says." Which fruit does Pinky pick?
steps: Find Pinky in the story.
The story says: Pinky picks a big mango.
So Pinky picks a mango.

learn.reallife: At the market, the fruit seller has mangoes and bananas. The sabzi seller has potatoes and onions.

quiz.q: Which one is a fruit?
quiz.explain: A banana is a fruit. Potato and onion are vegetables.
steps: A banana is a fruit.
Potato and onion are vegetables.
Answer: Banana
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fruits and vegetables

quiz.q: Which one is a vegetable?
quiz.explain: Spinach (palak) is a leafy vegetable.
steps: Spinach (palak) is a leafy vegetable.
Guava and grapes are fruits.
Answer: Spinach
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fruits and vegetables

quiz.q: Which is the national fruit of India?
quiz.explain: The mango is the national fruit of India.
steps: India has a national fruit.
It is the mango.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the national fruit

quiz.q: Read: "Papa buys green spinach and orange carrots." What colour are the carrots?
quiz.explain: The line says orange carrots. Green tells about the spinach.
steps: Read the line: orange carrots.
So the carrots are orange. Green goes with spinach.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which colour goes with which word

quiz.q: Read: "She sees red apples and yellow bananas." What colour are the bananas?
quiz.explain: The line says yellow bananas.
steps: Read the line: yellow bananas.
So the bananas are yellow. Red goes with apples.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which colour goes with which word

quiz.q: 🥭 Which is the right spelling for this fruit?
quiz.explain: We spell it m-a-n-g-o: mango.
steps: Say the letters: m-a-n-g-o.
So the spelling is mango.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong vowel

teach.ask: Gappu: Is a mango a fruit or a vegetable? What about a potato?
teach.praise: Yum! Now I know fruits from vegetables!
teach.nudge: Can you name a fruit and a vegetable?

revise.summary: Mango, banana, apple and guava are fruits. Potato, carrot, spinach and onion are vegetables. The mango is the national fruit of India.
focus: Sort foods into fruits and vegetables
Read a line to find the colour of a food
Spell fruit names like mango
remember: Fruits: mango, banana, apple, guava, papaya, grapes
Vegetables: potato, carrot, spinach, onion, brinjal, cauliflower
The mango is the national fruit of India
traps: Don't mix up fruits and vegetables: spinach is a vegetable.
Match each colour word with the word right after it.

learn.hook: Want to run fast and grow strong? Eat well!
points: Fruits, vegetables, dal, rice, roti and milk help us grow.
Drink clean water many times a day.
Wash your hands before you eat.
Chips, sweets and cold drinks are fine only once in a while.
Eat slowly and chew your food well.

example.q: Think it through: Ravi wants a healthy snack after school. Should he pick a banana or a big packet of chips?
steps: A banana is a fruit. Fruits help us stay healthy.
Chips have a lot of salt and oil.
So the banana is the healthier snack.

learn.reallife: A good lunch box can have roti, sabzi and a fruit like a guava or an apple.

games.title: Healthy or not? True or false?
items: We should wash our hands before we eat.
Washing hands removes dirt and germs.
Fruits and vegetables help us stay healthy.
Eating chips at every meal is healthy.
Chips have a lot of salt and oil. Eat them only sometimes.
Our body needs water every day.
It is good to gulp food without chewing.
We should chew our food well.

games.title: Every day or once in a while?

quiz.q: What should we do before eating?
quiz.explain: Clean hands keep germs away from our food.
steps: Our hands can have germs.
So we wash our hands before we eat.
quiz.mistake: Forgets about washing hands

quiz.q: Which is a healthy snack?
quiz.explain: An apple is a fruit. It is a healthy snack.
steps: An apple is a fruit.
Fruits are healthy snacks. Chips and cold drinks are only once in a while.
Answer: An apple
quiz.mistake: Thinks tasty packaged food is healthy

quiz.q: What should we drink many times a day?
quiz.explain: Our body needs clean water every day.
steps: Our body needs water every day.
So we drink clean water many times a day.
quiz.mistake: Thinks cold drinks are as good as water

quiz.q: Read: "Meena eats roti, dal and a guava for lunch." Which fruit does Meena eat?
quiz.explain: Guava is the fruit. Roti and dal are not fruits.
steps: Meena eats roti, dal and a guava.
Guava is the fruit. Roti and dal are not fruits.
quiz.mistake: Picks food that is not a fruit

quiz.q: How should we eat our food?
quiz.explain: Chewing food well helps our body use it.
steps: We should eat slowly.
We chew our food well.
Answer: Slowly, chewing it well
quiz.mistake: Thinks eating fast is good

quiz.q: Healthy food helps us ___.
quiz.explain: Healthy food helps our body grow strong.
steps: Healthy food is good for our body.
It helps us grow strong.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up healthy and unhealthy

teach.ask: Gappu: I only want to eat sweets! Is that okay?
teach.praise: Okay! A fruit for me, and a sweet only sometimes!
teach.nudge: What should I eat every day to grow strong?

revise.summary: Fruits, vegetables, dal, rice, roti and milk help us grow. We drink clean water, wash hands before eating and chew food well.
focus: Pick the healthy snack
Know good habits before and while eating
Know which foods to have only once in a while
remember: Wash your hands before you eat
Drink clean water many times a day
Eat slowly and chew your food well
traps: Don't think tasty chips or cold drinks are healthy. Have them only once in a while.
Cold drinks are not as good as water.

learn.hook: Do you like karela? Some do, some don't. That is okay!
points: We say "I like ..." for things we enjoy.
We say "I do not like ..." or "I don't like ..." for things we do not enjoy.
We ask "Do you like ...?" to find out.
We answer "Yes, I do." or "No, I don't."

example.q: Read: Asha: "Do you like idli?" Sam: "Yes, I do. I like idli with sambar." Does Sam like idli?
steps: Asha asks a question.
Sam says, "Yes, I do."
So Sam likes idli.

learn.reallife: At a birthday party, friends ask each other, "Do you like cake?"

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

quiz.q: Read: "I like grapes. I don't like onions." What does the child like?
quiz.explain: The child says, "I like grapes."
steps: The child says, 'I like grapes.'
So the child likes grapes. Don't like onions means no to onions.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word don't

quiz.q: Read: "I like grapes. I don't like onions." What does the child not like?
quiz.explain: "I don't like onions" means the child does not enjoy onions.
steps: Look for don't: 'I don't like onions.'
So the child does not like onions.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word don't

quiz.q: Your friend asks, "Do you like milk?" You do. What do you say?
quiz.explain: To answer "Do you like...?" with yes, we say "Yes, I do."
steps: You like milk, so the answer is yes.
For 'Do you like...?' we say, 'Yes, I do.'
quiz.mistake: Uses am instead of do in the short answer

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.explain: With I, we say like: I like dosa.
steps: With I, we say like.
So: I like dosa. Not likes, not liking.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s after I

quiz.q: Which word means the same as "do not"?
quiz.explain: Don't is the short form of do not.
steps: Do not has a short form.
The short form is don't.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the short form don't

quiz.q: Riya does not like karela. What is kind to say?
options: That is okay. I like it.
quiz.explain: People can like different foods. We speak kindly about it.
steps: People can like different foods.
So we speak kindly: 'That is okay. I like it.'
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is fine to tease others about likes

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I tell my friend what food I like?
teach.praise: I like you! You are a great teacher!
teach.nudge: What do I say for food I do not like?

revise.summary: We say 'I like ...' for things we enjoy and 'I don't like ...' for things we do not. We ask 'Do you like ...?' and answer 'Yes, I do.' or 'No, I don't.'
focus: Tell what someone likes and does not like
Answer 'Do you like ...?' the right way
Use I like, not I likes
remember: I like ... / I do not like ... / I don't like ...
Do you like ...? - Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Don't is the short form of do not
traps: Don't miss the word don't. It changes the meaning.
Don't say 'Yes, I am.' Say 'Yes, I do.'
Don't say 'I likes'. Say 'I like'.

learn.hook: Hot, wet, cold or full of flowers? Every season is different!
points: Summer is hot. The sun shines bright.
The rainy season brings dark clouds and lots of rain.
After the rains, autumn comes. Then comes winter, which is cold.
Spring comes after winter. Many plants have new leaves and flowers.
The seasons come again and again, every year.

example.q: Read the poem: "Summer sun is hot and bright. Rainy clouds bring rain at night. Winter mornings, cold and grey. Spring brings flowers, hip hooray!" Which season brings flowers?
steps: Find the word flowers in the poem.
The line is: Spring brings flowers.
So spring brings flowers.

learn.reallife: We eat cool mangoes in summer, jump in puddles in the rainy season and drink hot soup in winter.

games.title: Season after season
games.prompt: Start with summer. Which season comes next?

games.title: Seasons: true or false?
items: In summer, the sun is very hot.
It rains a lot in the rainy season.
That is why it is called the rainy season.
After the cold winter, spring comes.
There is only one season in a year.
A year has many seasons, one after another.

quiz.q: Read: "Summer sun is hot and bright." What is the summer sun like?
quiz.explain: The line says the summer sun is hot and bright.
steps: Read the line: summer sun is hot and bright.
So the summer sun is hot and bright. Cold and grey is winter.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up summer and winter

quiz.q: Read: "Winter mornings, cold and grey." Which season has cold mornings?
quiz.explain: The line says winter mornings are cold.
steps: Read the line: winter mornings, cold and grey.
So winter has cold mornings.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up summer and winter

quiz.q: Read: "Rainy clouds bring rain at night." What do the clouds bring?
quiz.explain: The line says rainy clouds bring rain.
steps: Read the line: rainy clouds bring rain at night.
So the clouds bring rain.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Read: "Summer sun is hot and bright." Which word rhymes with bright?
quiz.explain: Bright and night both end with the sound -ight.
steps: Bright ends with the sound -ight.
Night also ends with -ight. So night rhymes with bright.
quiz.mistake: Picks any word from the line

quiz.q: Which season comes after winter?
quiz.explain: After winter comes spring.
steps: Winter is cold.
Spring comes after winter, with new leaves and flowers.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the order of seasons

quiz.q: Which is the opposite of hot?
quiz.explain: Hot and cold are opposites.
steps: Hot and cold are opposites.
Warm is close to hot, so it is not the opposite.
Answer: Cold
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with a similar meaning

teach.ask: Gappu: What are seasons? Is it always hot?
teach.praise: Sunny, rainy, chilly or flowery - I know them all now!
teach.nudge: Which season is hot and which is cold?

revise.summary: Summer is hot, the rainy season brings rain, autumn comes after the rains, winter is cold, and spring brings new leaves and flowers. The seasons come again every year.
focus: Know what each season is like
Know which season comes after winter
Read a line of a poem and find rhyming words
remember: Summer: hot. Rainy season: rain. Winter: cold. Spring: flowers.
Spring comes after winter
Hot and cold are opposites
traps: Don't mix up summer (hot) and winter (cold).
Warm is not the opposite of hot. Cold is.

learn.hook: Would you wear a sweater on a hot day? No way!
points: Weather words: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot and cold.
On hot days we wear light cotton clothes and a cap.
On rainy days we use a raincoat and an umbrella.
On cold days we wear a woollen sweater, a cap and socks.
We dress to keep our body comfortable.

example.q: Think it through: It is raining hard. Tara has to go to school. What should she take?
steps: Rain will make her wet.
A raincoat or an umbrella keeps us dry.
So Tara should take an umbrella or wear a raincoat.

learn.reallife: In Delhi winters, children wear sweaters to school. In Chennai summers, they wear light cotton clothes.

items.q: When rain falls, the day is ___
When the sun shines, the day is ___
We hold it over our head in rain
A warm top made of wool

quiz.q: It is a cold winter morning. What should Rohan wear?
quiz.explain: Woollen clothes keep us warm when it is cold.
steps: It is a cold morning.
A woollen sweater keeps us warm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up clothes for hot and cold weather

quiz.q: It is a very hot summer day. What is best to wear?
quiz.explain: Cotton clothes are light and cool for hot days.
steps: It is a very hot day.
Light cotton clothes keep us cool. Woollen clothes are for cold days.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up clothes for hot and cold weather

quiz.q: What do we use to stay dry in the rain?
quiz.explain: An umbrella keeps the rain off us.
steps: Rain makes us wet.
An umbrella keeps the rain off us.
quiz.mistake: Does not match the thing to the weather

quiz.q: Read: "The wind blows the kites high in the sky." What is the weather like?
quiz.explain: Wind blowing hard means it is windy.
steps: The clue word is wind.
When the wind blows hard, it is windy.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue word wind

quiz.q: 🌧️ Which is the right spelling for water falling from clouds?
quiz.explain: We spell it r-a-i-n: rain.
steps: Say the letters: r-a-i-n.
So the spelling is rain.
quiz.mistake: Writes the word the way it sounds

quiz.q: The sky is full of dark clouds. Which word fits?
quiz.explain: When clouds cover the sky, it is cloudy.
steps: The clue is dark clouds in the sky.
When clouds cover the sky, it is cloudy.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue in the sentence

teach.ask: Gappu: It is cold outside! What should I wear? What about when it rains?
teach.praise: Brrr... I am wearing my sweater now! Thank you!
teach.nudge: What do I wear when it is cold or rainy?

revise.summary: Weather can be sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot or cold. We wear cotton on hot days, a raincoat or umbrella on rainy days and woollens on cold days.
focus: Pick the right clothes for the weather
Use clue words to name the weather
Spell weather words like rain
remember: Hot day: light cotton clothes and a cap
Rainy day: raincoat and umbrella
Cold day: woollen sweater, cap and socks
traps: Don't mix up clothes for hot and cold days.
Don't miss the clue word: wind means windy, dark clouds mean cloudy.

learn.hook: Sun plus rain can paint the sky! Have you seen a rainbow?
points: A rainbow has seven colours.
The colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
We can remember them as VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
We can see a rainbow when the sun shines while it rains, or just after rain.
Never look straight at the sun. It can hurt your eyes.

example.q: Read: "It was a grey, rainy day. Pari looked out of the window. The sun came out and the rain was still falling. A rainbow! Pari took her crayons and drew it with all seven colours." How many colours did Pari use?
steps: Find the part about Pari's drawing.
It says she drew it with all seven colours.
A rainbow has seven colours.

learn.reallife: We can see rainbow colours in the spray of a garden pipe on a sunny day, and in soap bubbles too.

games.title: Rainbow: true or false?
items: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
Green is a colour of the rainbow.
Green is in the middle of VIBGYOR.
Pink is one of the seven rainbow colours.
We can see a rainbow when the sun shines and it rains.
Sunlight and raindrops make a rainbow.
It is safe to look straight at the sun.
Looking at the sun can hurt our eyes.

quiz.q: How many colours are in a rainbow?
quiz.explain: A rainbow has seven colours: VIBGYOR.
steps: A rainbow has seven colours.
VIBGYOR has 7 letters: 7 colours.
quiz.mistake: Does not remember the number of colours

quiz.q: Which colour is in the rainbow?
quiz.explain: Indigo is the I in VIBGYOR. Brown and black are not rainbow colours.
steps: VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
Indigo is the I. Brown and black are not in the rainbow.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every colour is in the rainbow

quiz.q: In VIBGYOR, what does G stand for?
quiz.explain: G stands for green.
steps: VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
G stands for green.
quiz.mistake: Picks another colour that begins with G

quiz.q: Read: "The sun came out and the rain was still falling." What may Pari see in the sky now?
quiz.explain: Sun and rain together can make a rainbow.
steps: The sun is out and the rain is still falling.
Sun and rain together can make a rainbow.
quiz.mistake: Does not link sun and rain to a rainbow

quiz.q: Read: "It was a grey, rainy day." What was the day like?
quiz.explain: The line says it was a grey, rainy day.
steps: Read the line: it was a grey, rainy day.
So the day was grey and rainy.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: 🍊 Which is the right spelling for this colour?
quiz.explain: We spell it o-r-a-n-g-e: orange.
steps: Say the letters: o-r-a-n-g-e.
So the spelling is orange.
quiz.mistake: Writes the word the way it sounds

teach.ask: Gappu: I saw a rainbow! What colours were in it?
teach.praise: Seven colours! VIBGYOR! I will remember it!
teach.nudge: How many colours does a rainbow have?

revise.summary: A rainbow has seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red (VIBGYOR). We can see one when the sun shines while it rains.
focus: Know the seven rainbow colours
Say what each letter of VIBGYOR stands for
Know when we can see a rainbow
remember: A rainbow has 7 colours
VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
Never look straight at the sun
traps: Don't think every colour is in the rainbow. Brown and black are not.
G in VIBGYOR is green, not grey.

learn.hook: Close your eyes. Can you see a purple elephant? That is imagination!
points: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
We can draw what we imagine: a flying fish or a pink tiger!
Colour words tell about things: a red kite, a blue sky.
We can tell about our drawing: "This is my house. It has a red door."
Every drawing is special. There is no wrong way to imagine.

example.q: Think it through: Pari wants to draw a rainbow. What should she do first, and what last?
steps: First, she takes paper and crayons.
Next, she draws the curved lines and colours each one.
Last, she shows her drawing to her friends.
example.answer: First get paper and crayons; last show the drawing.

learn.reallife: On Children's Day or in art class, we draw and colour pictures and put them on the wall.

games.title: Let us draw
games.prompt: Put the drawing steps in order.

quiz.q: What does imagine mean?
options: To make a picture in your mind
quiz.explain: When we imagine, we see a picture in our mind.
steps: Imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
It does not mean to sleep or run.
Answer: To make a picture in your mind
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of imagine

quiz.q: Read: "Pari drew a big yellow sun." Which word tells the colour?
quiz.explain: Yellow is the colour word. Big tells size.
steps: Yellow is a colour word.
Big tells the size. Sun is the thing.
Answer: Yellow
quiz.mistake: Mixes up colour and size words

quiz.q: Read: "Pari drew a big yellow sun." Who drew the sun?
quiz.explain: The line says Pari drew it.
steps: Read the line: Pari drew a big yellow sun.
Pari is the person. So Pari drew the sun.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that is not a person

quiz.q: What do we use to colour a picture?
quiz.explain: We colour with crayons or colour pencils.
steps: We colour with crayons or colour pencils.
A spoon and a pillow are not for colouring.
Answer: Crayons
quiz.mistake: Does not know drawing tools

quiz.q: Which sentence tells about a drawing?
quiz.explain: "This is my red kite" is a correct sentence about a drawing.
steps: 'This is my red kite.' has words in the right order.
It tells about a drawing. 'Kite my is red this' is mixed up.
Answer: This is my red kite.
quiz.mistake: Picks a sentence with words in the wrong order

quiz.q: Blue paint and yellow paint mixed together make ___.
quiz.explain: Blue and yellow paint mix to make green.
steps: Mix blue paint with yellow paint.
The two colours make green.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a colour without knowing colour mixing

teach.ask: Gappu: What does imagine mean? How do I draw what I imagine?
teach.praise: I imagined a rainbow Gappu! You helped me!
teach.nudge: What does it mean to imagine?

revise.summary: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind. We can draw what we imagine, use colour words, and tell about our drawing.
focus: Know the meaning of imagine
Find the colour word in a sentence
Tell about a drawing in a correct sentence
remember: Imagine: make a picture in your mind
Tell about a drawing: This is my house. It has a red door.
There is no wrong way to imagine
traps: Don't mix up colour words (yellow) and size words (big).
Don't put words in the wrong order: say 'This is my red kite.'
